story:
The path ended here, at the edge of the pond, where someone long ago decided a lantern should stand.

It sits on three curved legs like a patient wading bird, its roof the same weathered grey as the stones around it. Nothing about it is in a hurry. The gravel in front has been raked smooth, the maples overhead are in full summer green, and the water holds the whole scene upside down.

I waited for a while to see if anything would move. Nothing did, and that was the point. (AI Description)

title: Star Icosahedron frosted
story:
Noot a gemstone, though it wants to be one.

This is an icosahedron, twenty faces of pure geometry, rendered in a green that sits somewhere between emerald and deep sea water. Look closely and the faces are not flat: smaller facets fold inward, as if the shape were cut from the inside as well as the outside. Light seems to travel down into it and not come back out.

A reminder that a shape can be perfectly regular and still keep a few secrets. (AI Description)

title: m16 v3 4k
story:
Seven thousand light-years away, a cloud of gas is quietly building stars.

The blue-white glow at the centre is where young, hot stars are lighting the gas around them. Dark ridges of dust frame it, and near the middle you can just make out the slender columns astronomers call the Pillars of Creation, each one a nursery thousands of times wider than our solar system.

The light in this frame left long before anyone pointed a telescope at it. Every colour here is a different element glowing at its own wavelength, and the thousands of small stars in the foreground are just company on the way. (AI Description)
